A.explanation: This describes part of a vector but omits the unit, so a value like $5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ north could not be fully stated.

B.explanation: A physical quantity is a measurable quantity stated as a numerical magnitude together with its unit, such as $3.0 \text{ kg}$.

C.explanation: This describes a scalar quantity, but it omits the unit and excludes vector quantities which also are physical quantities.

D.explanation: A unit alone such as $\text{metre}$ has no meaning without a numerical magnitude to say how many units are present.

hints: Look at which of the words magnitude, direction and unit appear together in each of options A to D.
Recall that a measurement such as $4.5 \text{ m}$ needs both a number and a unit, while direction is only added for vector quantities.
Check which option applies to both scalars and vectors and gives a complete measurement with no missing part.
walkthrough: Identify what the question asks: the general definition of any physical quantity, not just scalars or just vectors.
Recall the rule: a physical quantity = numerical magnitude x unit, for example $2.5 \text{ A}$ or $10 \text{ m}$.
Note that direction is required only for vectors such as velocity, so it cannot be part of the general definition.
Therefore magnitude plus unit is necessary and sufficient for all physical quantities.
